findings.text: Public KASLR placement service. When the disable option is present it leaves outputs unchanged. Otherwise it marks the boot header as randomized, establishes a word-size dependent physical limit, records regions that must be avoided, derives an aligned lower bound from the smaller of the supplied output and a fixed half-gigabyte ceiling, obtains a randomized physical load address and a randomized virtual base on 64-bit, and updates the supplied physical output only on success.

Physical randomization succeeds only with a range fully inside the global limit and without an oversized static map table. Source preference is handover scratch areas when handover data exists, otherwise firmware memory map when its signature and placement are acceptable, otherwise the legacy RAM map. The chosen candidate must again satisfy the requested bounds or the attempt fails with a diagnostic and a zero result.

Firmware map randomization is enabled only when the loader signature matches one of two expected values and, on 32-bit, when the map resides below four gigabytes. A preliminary scan records whether any mirrored descriptor exists. Usable descriptors are limited to free types with soft-reserved entries excluded when that feature is active and, when mirroring was observed, to mirrored entries only. Each survivor contributes its physical base and page-count derived length as a candidate region.

Free firmware memory comprises conventional type unconditionally plus unaccepted type only when the corresponding build option is enabled. All other types are treated as unavailable for randomization.
Legacy map randomization considers only entries classified as RAM, exposing each as a base plus length region to the shared region evaluator until that evaluator signals completion.

Handover randomization is inactive without handover support or without a setup chain entry of the handover type yielding a non-empty scratch array. When active, every scratch area supplies its stored base and length as a candidate region to the shared evaluator until completion, and overall success reports that handover sources were consumed.

Virtual randomization outcome always lies on physical-alignment granularity within the interval from the supplied minimum up to the kernel image size minus the image length. The number of alignment slots in that interval determines the modulus applied to a fresh random value, whose scaled result plus the minimum forms the returned base.

Randomization can abort collection when the immovable-region slot table fills or when more static map overrides than supported were supplied, emitting a diagnostic and failing the attempt. A final bounds check guards against an out-of-range random pick, also failing with a diagnostic rather than returning an unsafe address.

Platform dispatch for making a physical interval usable. Confidential guests route to their respective acceptance primitive, with one guest failure treated as fatal, while unrecognized platforms report an error instead of silently succeeding.

One guest detection result is build-gated and evaluated at most once, caching the outcome. Evaluation compares a fixed identification pattern against values returned from a dedicated processor identification leaf, treating equality as guest presence.

Secure nested paging guest status becomes sticky true only after the platform status register indicates the relevant enabled bit. On first success without a recorded privilege level, extended processor identification is consulted for secure-VM service support; when present the calling-area address is captured from its register and a non-zero placeholder level is recorded because acceptance does not depend on the exact level.

Processor encrypted-virtualization capability requires availability of the relevant extended identification range and the corresponding feature indicator. Failure yields a device-absent error. On success a flag records whether software fallback is required based on a high capability bit, and the low bits identifying the encryption position are returned.
Status accessor returning zero when processor support probing fails and otherwise the full contents of the platform status register.

Secure nested paging acceptance marks every page in the half-open interval as private through a descriptor bound to the recorded calling area, iterating in page granularity from start inclusive to end exclusive.
When secure nested paging support is compiled out, acceptance is a no-operation and guest detection constantly reports absence, allowing callers to remain unconditional.

Unaccepted-table discovery requires firmware boot, successful location of the configuration table, presence of the vendor table for unaccepted memory, and a recognized version, otherwise reporting absence or raising an error for unknown version or missing table. On success the global table pointer is refreshed before any acceptance use to cover stub relocation cases.

Early assembly query returning the page-table bit position used for encryption only when the extended identification range exists, the relevant feature is advertised, and the enabled indicator in the status register is set; all other cases yield zero while preserving the callee-saved register used during the query.

Encrypted-state processor identification exchange over the hypervisor communication register. A request encoding the desired result component is written, a VM exit is performed, then reserved response bits must be clear and the completion code must indicate identification success. Any deviation reports failure; otherwise success with the result delivered through the shared register.

32-bit exception entry for virtualization exceptions. It accepts only processor identification exits, collects all four result components through repeated hypervisor exchanges into the saved register area, enforces that the encrypted-virtualization range and feature remain visible when those leaves are queried, skips the faulting instruction and returns on success, and otherwise requests termination from the hypervisor before halting.

Early 32-bit descriptor table contains an entry for the virtualization exception vector pointing at the dedicated handler with kernel code selector and present 32-bit interrupt-gate attributes. Loading computes table addresses position-independently, installs that entry, and activates the table via its descriptor.

Encryption-bit validation is skipped when recorded status is zero. Otherwise two hardware random values are stored and paging plus protected mode are enabled to test whether ciphertext visibility alters them. Matching values restore the prior control register and continue, while any mismatch halts without progress to avoid running with an inconsistent encryption view.

Decompressor shared state consists of a pointer to boot parameters, port input-output operations, a bump allocation cursor with its end bound, a counter for stray non-maskable interrupts, and video output state comprising a memory base and a control port. Video state is file-local while the others have external linkage.

Early text output fans out to serial and video when each is available. Serial transmission polls a readiness indicator with bounded retries before writing. Video emission tracks cursor coordinates in boot parameters, wraps lines, scrolls by moving rows and clearing the last row, and updates the hardware cursor through paired port writes. Numeric helpers render unsigned values in hexadecimal with full width and decimal minimally through a common base-conversion routine that expands line feeds for serial.

Relocation need is determined by the difference between actual load address and linked physical base, refined on 64-bit to the virtual base difference; zero difference performs no work. Otherwise two zero-terminated tables stored backward from the image end are applied in order for narrow then wide locations, each entry translated from kernel virtual to the current mapping, range-checked against the decompressed span with fatal error on escape, and adjusted by the computed delta. A build without relocatable support provides an empty operation.

Kernel image placement validates the executable magic, materializes program headers in transient heap storage, enforces a large-page multiple alignment for load segments on 64-bit, copies each loadable segment to its relocated or absolute destination while ignoring other segment types, releases the temporary headers, and returns the entry offset relative to the linked base. Associated constants expose text length, init-text location and length, total span, and a statically aligned early heap.

Candidate region abstraction carries a start address and a length. Firmware descriptors supply base plus page-count derived length, legacy entries supply stored base plus stored length, and handover scratch entries supply stored address plus stored size, all evaluated through a common boolean completion predicate.

Boot layout facts: a randomization presence flag in load flags, a linked physical base, a kernel image size bounding virtual randomization, a physical alignment granularity for placement, and a maximum memory ceiling on 64-bit. Relocation validity spans from the output base through the end of uninitialized data.

Firmware and confidential-computing facts: loader signatures distinguishing firmware word sizes, RAM classification for legacy entries, handover setup type, free-type and reliability plus soft-reserve attributes with page-shift sizing, extended processor identification leaves for capability discovery, status and calling-area registers with enabled and nested-paging bits, hypervisor communication register with defined request and completion codes, virtualization exception vector and exit code for identification, and kernel code selector with interrupt-gate attributes.

Decompressor shorthand facts: a static qualifier alias, a malloc visibility marker, a zeroing helper mapped to setting memory, a move helper identity, and serial register facts comprising a transmitter-ready mask plus transmit and line-status offsets.
